sentences.text: Stangerochampsa was a small to medium-sized crocodyliform, with a type skull measuring 20.0 cm in length and 13.0 cm in width, and a thigh bone 14.2 cm long.
Its jaws featured heterodont dentition, a term for having different types of teeth, including large crushing teeth located at the rear.
The genus was first described in 1996 by Wu and colleagues.
The genus name honors the Stanger family, who owned the ranch where the specimen was found, while the species name honors James Ross McCabe, the discoverer and preparer of the fossil.
Stangerochampsa is classified within the unranked family Globidonta.
Recent studies have yielded conflicting placements, with the animal recovered as a stem-group caiman in 2021 and as a basal alligatorine in 2022.
The type specimen was discovered in the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian-age Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta.
Stangerochampsa lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Brochu (1999) suggested that Stangerochampsa and Albertochampsa were synonymous and placed the genus just outside the family Alligatoridae.
Later, Brochu (2004) and Hill and Lucas (2006) found Stangerochampsa outside of Alligatorinae, with Hill and Lucas identifying Albertochampsa as its sister taxon.
